subject: Accounts
title: Working notes = step marks
text: Show a working note for every adjustment, even a small one. If the final figure goes wrong, clear working notes still earn you step marks.

subject: Costing
title: Statement first, numbers later
text: In process costing, prepare the Statement of Equivalent Production before anything else. Once the units are right, the cost per unit and valuation follow easily.

subject: Law
title: Provision → Facts → Conclusion
text: Write every Law answer in three parts: the relevant provision, how it applies to the facts given, and a clear one-line conclusion. Examiners look for all three.

subject: Auditing
title: Remember SAs by series
text: Group the Standards on Auditing by series: 200s – general principles, 300s & 400s – risk assessment and response, 500s – audit evidence, 600s – using the work of others, 700s – reporting. Then learn the titles inside each series.

subject: Income Tax
title: Keep a one-page limits chart
text: Make a single page with all exemption and deduction limits you study, and revise it once a week. Most marks lost in tax come from a wrong limit, not a wrong concept.

subject: Financial Management
title: Formula first, then figures
text: In FM, write the formula before putting the numbers in. If there is a calculation slip, the correct formula alone can still earn marks.

subject: GST
title: Three questions for every GST problem
text: Before computing GST, ask: Is it a supply? Is it taxable or exempt? Where is the place of supply? The third answer tells you IGST, or CGST + SGST.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Use the case's own words
text: In SM case answers, use the company name and the facts given in the case, and name the model you are applying (BCG, Ansoff, Porter, SWOT). Generic textbook answers score less.

subject: Accounts
title: Format before figures
text: For long questions like amalgamation or consolidation, draw the format first (headings and columns), then fill in the figures. It saves time and avoids missing items.

subject: Costing
title: Know the sign of every variance
text: For each variance, learn what Favourable and Adverse mean in words, not just the formula. Writing (F) or (A) correctly is part of the answer.

subject: Law
title: One-line case laws
text: Keep a list of important case laws with one line of facts and one line of the decision. Quoting a relevant case makes a Law answer stand out.

subject: Auditing
title: Use audit keywords
text: Use standard phrases like 'sufficient appropriate audit evidence', 'professional scepticism' and 'material misstatement' in audit answers – they show the examiner you know the language of the SAs.

subject: Income Tax
title: Always show the heads of income
text: In computation questions, present income head by head with clear sub-totals, then deductions and tax. A well-laid-out computation is easier to mark and earns more.

subject: Financial Management
title: Don't miss the hidden cash flows
text: In capital budgeting, check for the tax saving on depreciation, the working capital released at the end and the salvage value. These are the cash flows students most often forget.

subject: GST
title: Goods vs services timing
text: Make a side-by-side table of time of supply rules for goods and for services. Seeing them together makes the differences easy to remember.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Draw the model
text: When a question asks about a matrix or framework, draw a small diagram (BCG boxes, Ansoff grid, Five Forces). A neat diagram explains in seconds what takes a paragraph to write.

subject: Accounts
title: Read the AS question twice
text: In Accounting Standards questions, first identify which AS applies and what the question actually asks (treatment, disclosure or both), then answer only that.

subject: Financial Management
title: Ratios need the right base
text: For every ratio, be clear what goes on top and what goes below (e.g. average or closing figures). Write the formula with the figures used – half the marks are in the presentation.

subject: Law
title: Practise MCQs on provisions
text: Law MCQs often test exact conditions – numbers of members, days or limits. Note such numbers in a separate list while reading.

subject: Costing
title: Classify before you calculate
text: Before solving a costing problem, classify each cost as direct or indirect, fixed or variable. Most costing mistakes start with a wrong classification.
